clue.text: Pope-like?

parts.note: the poet Alexander Pope wrote in the eighteenth-century style that revived Greek and Roman models, so a work like his belongs to that movement

explanation.walkthrough: Pope here is the English poet Alexander Pope, not the head of the Catholic Church; the question mark warns that the obvious reading is wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander Pope is the model poet of the eighteenth-century revival of classical forms, so being like him means following that revival.

clue.text: Begin to pontificate about Russia

indicators.note: the word for holding forth goes about, surrounding, the letter for Russia

parts.note: to spout is to hold forth pompously, as one who pontificates does
R is the international vehicle code for Russia

explanation.surface: Someone is about to start lecturing everyone on Russian affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts SPOUT around R.
explanation.definitionFit: Plants and ideas sprout when they start to grow, so the verb means to begin or come into being.

clue.text: Choose to take up one established mode as edifying

indicators.note: the word for choosing takes the next part inside it

parts.note: to cull is to pick out or select

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters run from bottom to top, read backwards

parts.note: A is the article meaning one
a rut is a fixed, settled way of doing things

explanation.surface: Picking a well-worn approach is presented as a way of improving the mind.
explanation.walkthrough: A + RUT turned 'up' gives TURA, which CULL 'takes' inside it: CUL-TURA-L.
explanation.definitionFit: Something edifying improves the mind, which is what activities relating to the arts and learning are meant to do.

clue.text: Cut tiles initially with pointed tool

parts.note: a style is a cut, as of hair or of a garment

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word tiles is taken

explanation.surface: Someone trims tiles using a sharp-pointed instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A stylet is a slender probe or engraving point, a small sharp instrument.

clue.text: Superior furs? Con's deceptive line

indicators.note: something deceptive misleads, so these letters are disguised in a new order

parts.note: the possessive s adds no letter; con is taken as written

explanation.surface: A fraudster sells supposedly luxury furs with a line of patter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deceptive' rearranges FURS and CON into SCORNFU; L follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Being scornful means looking down on others, the attitude of someone acting superior.

clue.text: Match fit

definitions.meaning: a sporting fixture or contest, as in an athletics gathering
suitable or proper, as in 'it is right and proper'

explanation.definitionFit: An athletics fixture is called a sports gathering of this name, and as an old adjective the word means suitable or proper.

clue.text: Trendy male injected drug

indicators.note: the letter for male is put into the word for trendy, like a needle's contents

parts.note: hep is an old slang word for fashionable, a variant of hip

explanation.surface: A fashionable man has been shot up with narcotics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'injected' puts M inside HEP.
explanation.definitionFit: Cannabis comes from the plant also used for rope fibre, so the plant's name serves for the narcotic.

clue.text: Not fast enough to make single

definitions.meaning: not fastened or tied to anything
not married or in a relationship

explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' means firmly fixed, not quick; 'enough to make' simply links the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means not fastened to anything, and also describes a person without a partner.

clue.text: Clumsy in practice no end

indicators.note: a clumsy arrangement is a botched one, so the letters that follow are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone who keeps fumbling every time they try is described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clumsy' rearranges PRACTICE NO END, and the whole clue describes the answer: someone always stumbling in practice.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who keeps having mishaps is constantly clumsy in everyday life.

clue.text: Puzzle over reduced credit in report

indicators.note: the word for over loses a letter, cut short at its end

parts.note: across can mean over, as in a bridge across or over a river

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the word for credit is given by its sound

parts.note: tick is British slang for credit, as in buying on tick

explanation.surface: Someone works on a puzzle, worried about their reduced credit rating in a report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' trims ACROSS to ACROS; TICK 'in report' is TIC.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a word puzzle in which the first letters of lines spell out a word.

clue.text: Like an instrument from baroque early time

indicators.note: baroque means extravagantly ornate, so the word early is twisted into a new form

explanation.surface: Something resembles an instrument from the early Baroque musical period.
explanation.walkthrough: 'baroque' rearranges EARLY into LYRA; T follows.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means shaped like a lyre, the ancient stringed instrument.

clue.text: All the players or the star?

parts.note: the cast is the whole company of actors in a show

explanation.surface: A question of whether credit goes to the whole company or to the leading actor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the star' looks like a theatre lead, but it is a real star, one of the twins in Gemini.
explanation.definitionFit: Castor is one of the two brightest stars in the constellation Gemini.

clue.text: Fellow in historic city in outstanding shopping area

indicators.note: that combination goes inside the word for outstanding

parts.note: due means owed and not yet paid, outstanding

indicators.note: the letter for fellow goes into the name of the old city

parts.note: Tyre is an ancient Phoenician city in modern Lebanon

explanation.surface: A man in an ancient city stands in an excellent place to shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts F into TYRE, and 'in' again puts TYFRE inside DUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Airport shops selling goods without tax form a retail zone named for that exemption.

clue.text: Requisites specified by primary school's head

parts.note: primary means fundamental or most important, as essential does

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A head teacher lists the things a primary school needs.
explanation.definitionFit: Requisites are the things required, the indispensable basics.

clue.text: Revivalist's means of influence, you might say

definitions.text: Revivalist's means of influence, you might say

parts.words: Revivalist's means of influence, you might say
parts.note: a revivalist is read as anything that brings a fainting person round, and its means of influence is a pungent whiff

explanation.walkthrough: A revivalist sounds like a preacher, but here it is whatever revives someone who has fainted.
explanation.definitionFit: A pungent ammonia preparation was held under a faint person's nose to bring them round, so it is literally a reviving agent.

clue.text: The plane's redesigned as a jumbo

indicators.note: the letters of the words are designed again into a new shape

parts.note: the possessive s adds no letter; plane is taken as written

explanation.surface: An aircraft has been rebuilt as a jumbo jet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redesigned' rearranges THE PLANE; 'jumbo' looks like a jet but means a big animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Jumbo was a famous zoo animal, and the name became a byword for the largest land mammal.

clue.text: South American writers with Poe's extreme tension

parts.note: US stands for American, as in US forces
pens are writing instruments

indicators.note: the extreme of a word is its end, here its final letter

explanation.surface: Writers from the Americas share Edgar Allan Poe's gift for nerve-racking stories.
explanation.definitionFit: Suspense is the anxious tension of waiting to see what happens.

clue.text: Bottle for team during break

indicators.note: the team comes during, inside, the word for a break

parts.note: a stop is a pause or break
a crew is a team of workers

explanation.surface: A team calls for a bottle during their tea break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' puts CREW inside STOP.
explanation.definitionFit: A bottle sealed with a threaded cap is called by the name of that kind of closure.

clue.text: Stupefied from hill fall when climbing

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, common on Dartmoor

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing means the word reads upward, so backwards

parts.note: a dip is a drop or fall

explanation.surface: A climber is left dazed after a fall on a hillside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when climbing' turns DIP into PID after TOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Torpid means sluggish and inactive, numbed in mind and body.

clue.text: Like certain birds as a rule found around northern Norway

indicators.note: the word for rule is found placed around the other letters

parts.note: sway is rule or dominion, as in holding sway
N is the international vehicle code for Norway

explanation.surface: Birds of a certain kind are said usually to live in the far north of Norway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found around' puts SWAY around NN.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means resembling a swan, the graceful long-necked water bird.

clue.text: Plant one tree? About fifty

indicators.note: the pieces go about, around, the numeral for fifty

parts.note: A is the article meaning one
a pine is a conifer tree
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether to plant one tree and settles on about fifty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' puts A PINE around L.
explanation.definitionFit: Mountain flowers adapted to high altitudes are a recognised class of garden plant.

clue.text: Pick up contract

definitions.meaning: to collect or to infer, as in 'I take it that...'
to draw together, as fabric pulled into folds

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to collect or to understand, and also to draw cloth into folds, pulling it together.

clue.text: A manner of life, showing off

parts.note: a way of life is a manner of living

explanation.surface: A lifestyle is shown off.
explanation.definitionFit: Being away means being absent or gone, as when someone is off on holiday.

clue.text: Given too much bread

parts.note: bread is slang for money, so this means handed too much cash, not too many loaves

explanation.walkthrough: 'bread' is old slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: A worker handed more wages than the job deserves has received excessive pay.

clue.text: Genteel property in Staines renovated by duke

indicators.note: the town is done up, so its letters are rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: Staines is a town in Surrey, west of London

explanation.surface: A refined house in the Surrey town of Staines has been done up by a duke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'renovated' rearranges IN STAINES into AINTINESS, after D.
explanation.definitionFit: Refined delicacy of manner is a quality, or property, that genteel people are expected to show.

clue.text: Duck on English river

parts.note: in cricket a duck is a score of zero, so nil

explanation.surface: A duck floats on an English river.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck in cricket is a batter's score of nought.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nile is the great river of north-east Africa.
